body.html: Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha overview — who it suits — To put it as simply as possible, Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha is a hotel and serviced apartment for people who want "a spacious room with a kitchen, a central location, and the sea within walking distance" on a budget that isn't too steep · It isn't a beachfront resort that lets you swim right out front, and it isn't a tiny boutique tucked down a quiet lane · Instead it's an in-town hotel building on Jerm Jompon Road in Si Racha Subdistrict, an easy walk from the seaside park and Ko Loi Si Racha · The hotel is part of the Cape & Kantary Hotels group, a Thai chain known for serviced-apartment rooms with in-room kitchens and a warm atmosphere · It has been open since 2007 and went through a renovation in 2022, so it has both the familiarity of a long-running hotel and the freshness of recently updated rooms · Real reviews line up on who this place fits: business travelers coming to work in the eastern industrial zone and the Japanese community in Si Racha, families who want a spacious room with a kitchen for a multi-day stay, and couples or working travelers who want a clean, central place at a price they can manage · Another group that calls it good value is people staying long, by the week or the month, since nearly every room type has a small kitchen, fridge, and cookware so it feels like home · If you're after a luxury beachfront resort with a quiet shore or a place right on the sand where you can swim immediately, this may not be the answer, and you'd be better off looking toward Bang Saen or Pattaya instead

Location and getting around — This is one of Cape Racha's top selling points, no question · The hotel sits on Jerm Jompon Road in central Si Racha, the old seaside quarter of town, which puts it genuinely within walking distance of the seaside park and the bayfront promenade in just a few minutes · Many reviews praise being able to walk out for morning exercise by the sea, find breakfast around the market, or stroll over to Ko Loi Si Racha, the town's landmark · Shopping and food are convenient too, since Robinson Si Racha is about a 5-minute drive away and the area around the hotel is full of restaurants, ramen shops, grill houses, and convenience stores, matching the large Japanese community that lives and works in this town · For working travelers, the hotel is a convenient drive from the industrial estates and Laem Chabang Port as well as the eastern industrial zones · Importantly, it's about a 25-30 min drive from Pattaya and a short drive from Bang Saen beach, which lets you use it as a base for both work and travel · Suvarnabhumi and U-Tapao airports are around 1-1.5 hours away · One small note is that the old-town streets of Si Racha get fairly busy with cars and motorbikes during rush hour, so if you're heading out to Laem Chabang or Pattaya in the morning, give yourself a little extra time, and while parking is free, it can get fairly tight when the hotel is full

"Great location, you can walk to the seafront and the park in just a few minutes. In the morning I'd go for a run along the bay and come back for breakfast at the hotel · The room was bigger than I expected, with a small kitchen so I could heat up my own food, only a five-minute drive to Robinson. Coming to work around Laem Chabang and staying here is the most convenient option."

Room types and decor — Cape Racha has around 194 rooms, most of them serviced-apartment style with in-room kitchens, which sets it apart from an ordinary in-town hotel in that "you can live in it like home" · The entry level is the Deluxe Studio and Studio Suite at around 46 sqm, which is considered very spacious for an entry room, with a sofa, a King bed or twin beds, plus a small kitchen and a separate sitting area · Stepping up is the One Bedroom Suite at around 61 sqm, with a clearly separated bedroom and living room, a full kitchen, and a bathroom with both a bathtub and a shower · There's also a Two Bedroom Suite for larger families or groups of friends traveling together · The decor is minimalist with warm earth tones, in keeping with the Cape & Kantary group's signature, focused on a clean look and real-world usability · Every room has a TV, fridge, kettle, cookware, blackout curtains, and the essentials · The point reviews praise most often is that the rooms are very clean and the floors aren't carpeted, so there are no problems with dust or musty smells, along with furniture that looks new after the 2022 renovation, and hot water that's strong and properly hot in the way Japanese guests like · For people coming to work or join online meetings, the in-room desk and the Wi-Fi signal are enough to get by · One note many reviews mention is that rooms in the annex building may not feel as good as the main building, and some room types are smaller than expected, so if size and newness matter to you, ask for a room in the main building or a recently renovated room right at the time of booking

Facilities, pool, and spa — The most talked-about highlight of Cape Racha is the outdoor rooftop swimming pool with the city and the Si Racha bay as a backdrop · Many reviews praise the pool being high up so you get distant sea views, with shaded corners to sit and rest, and it's a nice spot to photograph the sunset in the evening · The health and relaxation side is complete, with a gym, sauna, steam room, jacuzzi, and Cape Spa for anyone who wants to work out or get a relaxing massage after a day of sightseeing or work · Another corner many people like is the snooker-billiards room and the executive lounge for working or relaxing · On top of that there's a ballroom and meeting rooms for seminars and functions, free parking, and free Wi-Fi throughout · To be straight about it, from the reviews, some of the recreation equipment — like the ping-pong table and certain gym pieces — is starting to show its age, in line with a building that has been open since 2007 — so if you expect a gym and pool like a brand-new hotel, set your expectations accordingly, but in terms of the variety of facilities for the price, it offers more than an ordinary in-town hotel in the same area

Food and bars — The hotel has restaurants and a cafe with a fair bit of character · The main venue is Le Marin, a Mediterranean and international restaurant that serves set lunches and dinner, and is where the breakfast buffet is served · What sets Cape Racha apart from others is the breakfast, which a lot of reviews agree is varied and good quality, with Thai dishes, Japanese options to match the town's regular Japanese guests, and Western dishes, plus an egg station, salads, and coffee that earn praise · Another spot people mention is the Kantary cafe from the same group, with pastries, bakery items, cakes, and drinks, in a comfortable setting good for a late-morning coffee or for working · For other meals, the central location helps a lot, since the area around the hotel has local restaurants, Si Racha seafood spots, ramen shops, and convenience stores to choose from, so many people alternate between eating out and dining in the hotel — which is part of the charm of staying central and by the sea like this · One note some reviews bring up is that a few buffet dishes are served somewhat cold on some days, and refilling food during the rush can be a bit slow at times, but overall breakfast is a strong point that scores well among hotels in the same class

Service — Service is another area that draws fairly consistent praise in real reviews · The front-desk staff and many of the team are mentioned as polite, friendly, patient, and helpful, especially with early check-in when a room is available, recommending restaurants and places to visit in town, and looking after long-stay guests so they feel like familiar faces · The overall atmosphere of the hotel is quiet and unhurried, suited to people coming to work who want to genuinely rest · As part of the Cape & Kantary group with a large base of corporate and Japanese guests, the service standard is fairly steady and predictable · To be fair, there are some voices in the reviews saying that responsiveness at certain times or in certain departments may not be uniformly quick, especially when the hotel is full or there's a seminar on, but overall it's still a strong point that brings many guests back for repeat stays · The advice is that if you have a special request — such as a main-building room, a high-floor room with a sea view, or early check-in — let them know in advance and confirm again before you travel

What real reviews say (praise and criticism) — Pulling from Trip.com, Tripadvisor, Booking.com, and Priceline, the picture is fairly consistent on the positive side · On the praise side: a central location within walking distance of the sea and the park, rooms that are spacious and very clean especially after the 2022 renovation, rooms with kitchens that suit long stays and cooking your own meals, a varied, good-quality breakfast spanning Thai, Japanese, and Western dishes, a rooftop pool with city and bay views that has a nice evening atmosphere, hot water that's strong and properly hot, and friendly, attentive staff · In overall scores, Trip.com gives 9.0 from 126 reviews, Tripadvisor is at 4.4/5 from 94 reviews, and some platforms go as high as around 8.9 from several hundred reviews · On the watch-out side: what comes up is that some facilities are starting to show their age, such as the gym equipment and the ping-pong table, rooms in the annex building don't feel as good as the main building, some room types are smaller than expected, a few buffet dishes are served somewhat cold on some days, and street noise in rooms facing Jerm Jompon Road · Most of these criticisms can be addressed by choosing your room, asking for the main building, and setting your expectations right, rather than being a big problem that keeps people from coming back, and the high scores across several platforms show that the strengths outweigh the weaknesses in the eyes of most guests

"The room was very clean, the furniture looked new, the hot water was nice and hot the way I like it, and the breakfast was varied with Japanese dishes too · The only downside was getting a room in the annex building that felt a bit older than the main building, plus some of the gym equipment was old. Next time I'll ask for a main-building room with a sea view instead."

Price and value comparison — The entry price for a studio is around ฿2,100/night in the normal range, moving up depending on the season and room type · A larger room like the One Bedroom Suite at around 61 sqm runs from around ฿2,600 up, while the Two Bedroom Suite is higher than that depending on size and number of guests · Compared with other hotels and serviced apartments in Si Racha town, Cape Racha feels like good value in terms of room space and kitchen for the price, especially if you get a recently renovated room in the main building, and it suits long stays very well since the kitchen lets you cook your own meals and save on food costs · What adds to the value is the fairly extensive facilities — the rooftop pool, gym, sauna, jacuzzi, spa, snooker room, and free parking — which aren't easy to find in a hotel at the same price, plus a walk-to-the-sea location that's rare in this town · If you're planning to use Si Racha as a base for work in the industrial zone, for a long family stay, or for day trips to Pattaya and Bang Saen, a central room with a kitchen at this price is genuinely substantial, in exchange for accepting that the building has some age and not every detail is brand new

Things to know before booking — A few things help make the stay smoother · One, if newness and size matter to you, ask for a room in the main building or one renovated in 2022 right at booking, since reviews say annex-building rooms don't feel the same · Two, if you're staying several days or coming as a group, choosing a suite with a full kitchen is more worthwhile and convenient, letting you cook and heat up your own food like at home · Three, if you want a sea view and a nice atmosphere, ask for a high-floor room and leave time to head up to the rooftop pool in the evening to watch the sunset over the bay · Four, if you're sensitive to noise, rooms facing Jerm Jompon Road may pick up some traffic noise, so try asking for an interior or high-floor room · Five, parking is free but can get tight at times when the hotel is full or there's a seminar on, so ask in advance · Six, rooms fill up fast during long weekends and the high season, so book ahead, compare prices across several platforms, and choose a free-cancellation option if your plans aren't firm yet

Verdict — From all the real reviews, Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha is the hotel and serviced apartment best suited to people who want a spacious room with a kitchen, a central Si Racha location, and the sea within walking distance on an affordable budget, whether you're coming to work in the eastern industrial zone, on a long family stay, or using it as a base for day trips to Pattaya and Bang Saen · The 46 sqm studios up to suites with kitchens, the rooftop pool over the bay, the gym, sauna, jacuzzi, spa, the Le Marin Mediterranean restaurant, the Kantary cafe, and a location within walking distance of the seaside park and Ko Loi make it good value in terms of space and location for the price, to the point that an in-town rival isn't easy to find · If you're looking for a luxury beachfront resort where you can swim right away, or you need a brand-new room and a fully modern gym, you may need to make peace with the building's age and should consider a resort in Bang Saen or Pattaya instead · But for a trip where you want a good-value room with a kitchen in central Si Racha plus a walk to the sea — Cape Racha is a choice that meets that need well, and it's the reason it scores as high as 9.0 from real reviews on Trip.com and remains a place many regular guests return to

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha

faq.q: Where is Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha · can you really walk to the sea?
faq.a: The hotel is at 35 Jerm Jompon Road, Si Racha Subdistrict, Si Racha District, Chonburi, in central Si Racha · You can genuinely walk to the seaside park, the bayfront promenade, and Ko Loi Si Racha in just a few minutes · It's near Surasak Park (~260 m) and about a 5-minute drive to Robinson Si Racha · Near the Laem Chabang industrial estate and port, and about a 25-30 min drive from Pattaya and Bang Saen beach

faq.q: What is Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha's starting price · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at around ฿2,100/night for a studio of about 46 sqm in the normal range · There are Deluxe Studio and Studio Suite at around 46 sqm, One Bedroom Suite at around 61 sqm with a separate bedroom and full kitchen, up to a Two Bedroom Suite for larger families · Nearly every room has an in-room kitchen, good for long stays, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha for?
faq.a: It's very well suited to business travelers coming to work in the eastern industrial zone and the Japanese community in Si Racha, families who want a spacious room with a kitchen, and people staying long by the week, since nearly every room has an in-room kitchen · It's also convenient as a base for day trips to Pattaya and Bang Saen · If you're looking for a luxury beachfront resort where you can swim right away, a resort in Bang Saen or Pattaya may suit you better

faq.q: What swimming pool and facilities does Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha have?
faq.a: There's an outdoor rooftop swimming pool with city and Si Racha bay views · There's a gym, sauna, steam room, jacuzzi, Cape Spa, a snooker-billiards room, an executive lounge, a ballroom and meeting rooms, and free parking · There's the Le Marin Mediterranean restaurant and a Kantary cafe from the same group

faq.q: What are the rooms and cleanliness like at Cape Racha · how should you prepare?
faq.a: Most reviews praise that the rooms are spacious and very clean, the floors aren't carpeted so there are no dust problems, and the hot water is strong, especially after the 2022 renovation · The note is that rooms in the annex building don't feel as good as the main building and some rooms are smaller than expected → it's recommended to ask for a main-building room or a recently renovated one right at booking, and ask for a high-floor room if you want a sea view and to avoid street noise

faq.q: Is Cape Racha Hotel Sriracha still open · what's the review score?
faq.a: It's still open and operating normally · Open since 2007 and renovated in 2022 · The latest score is 9.0 from 126 reviews on Trip.com and 4.4/5 from 94 reviews on Tripadvisor, with many reviews praising the walk-to-the-sea location, spacious rooms with kitchens, cleanliness, and breakfast · The main note is the building's age and some facilities starting to show wear, so compare several sources before deciding
